meta.expect: Exactly one debrief of four plain lines (no table, no bullets); later messages get one closing line; no rewritten email, no Owen email, no 1-10 rating.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so let's start with who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and why I found out about it from my son's phone.
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk through the version history.
You haven't told me who decided on the zero, Hale. Version history of what, and did you look at it before or after the zero went into the gradebook?
612 words in one edit at 11:52 PM, then 794 more at 11:58 PM.
I'm writing down 11:52 and 11:58. What date was that, and which account is it from? Turn the screen.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and the date and account behind the times you gave me. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Opening position, with nothing agreed; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the date and account behind the times you gave her.
What moved her: Nothing yet; the times were specific, but with no date or account she had nothing she could check.
What cost ground: You went straight to the version history without answering who decided on the zero or why she found out from Owen's phone, so she stayed on procedure.
Try next time: Open with a sentence owning that the zero went in before you called her, then give the date and account alongside the times before she has to ask.
Redo the debrief as a table please.
The meeting is over. To practise again, start a new chat and paste the first message from the README.
Write the email Owen should send me to apologize.
